title: רעידת האדמה בכרתים (1856)
wikitext:
{{אסון טבע
| מפה = {{מממו|יוון|כרתים|סוג=רעידת אדמה}}
}}
'''רעידת האדמה בכרתים''' או '''רעידת האדמה בהרקליון''' התרחשה בבוקר [[12 באוקטובר]] [[1856]] בשעה 02:45 בבוקר. [[רעידת אדמה|רעידת האדמה]] הייתה ב[[עוצמה סייסמית|עוצמה]] מוערכת של בין 7.7 ל-8.3 ב[[סולם מגניטודה לפי מומנט]] בעומק של כ-61 עד 100 ק"מ.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Seismicity Catalog (550 B.C. - 2010)|url=http://geophysics.geo.auth.gr/the_seisnet/WEBSITE_2005/station_index_en.html|access-date=4 January 2021|website=Seismological Station|location=Aristotle University of Thessaloniki}}</ref> רעידת האדמה הורגשה על פני שטח רחב מאוד המשתרע מ[[סיציליה]] ב[[איטליה]] ועד ה[[לבנט]] וצפון [[צפון אפריקה|אפריקה]]. באי [[יוון|היווני]] [[כרתים]], השפעות רעידת האדמה היו חמורות, ומעל 500 בני אדם נהרגו בעיר [[הרקליון]]. גלי הלם מרעידת האדמה הורגשו בכל [[האימפריה העות'מאנית]], [[טורקיה]], [[קפריסין]] ו[[המזרח התיכון]]. ב[[מלטה]], רעידת האדמה הקריסה את [[מגדל Għajn Ħadid]] {{אנ|Għajn Ħadid Tower}} – מגדל שמירה על החוף שנבנה בסביבות שנת 1638. ב[[קהיר]] שבמצרים, רעידת האדמה הרסה מבנים, יצרה [[סייש]]ים בתעלות וגרמה להרוגים. מול חופי [[מצרים]] ו[[איטליה]] דיווחו מלחים שחשו ב[[רעידת ים]] {{אנ|Submarine earthquake}}.<ref name="PAPADOPOULOS">{{Cite journal|last=G. A. PAPADOPOULOS, E. DASKALAKI, A. FOKAEFS and N. GIRALEAS|title=TSUNAMI HAZARD IN THE EASTERN MEDITERRANEAN SEA: STRONG EARTHQUAKES AND TSUNAMIS IN THE WEST HELLENIC ARC AND TRENCH SYSTEM|url=http://www.seahellarc.gr/files/20091123154851Papadopoulos_et_al.JET.pdf|url-status=dead|journal=Journal of Earthquake and Tsunami|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304001548/http://www.seahellarc.gr/files/20091123154851Papadopoulos_et_al.JET.pdf|archive-date=2016-03-04|access-date=2021-01-04}}</ref>

== רקע טקטוני ==
לאורך החוף הדרומי של [[האיים הדודקאנסיים|איי דודקאנס]], [[רודוס]], [[כרתים]] ו[[האיים היוניים]], [[הלוח האפריקאי]] העשוי מקרום אוקיינוס [[הפחתה|הופחת]] מתחת ל[[לוח הים האגאי]] {{אנ|Aegean Sea plate}} (חלק מהלוח [[הלוח האירואסייתי|האירואסיאתי]]) בקצב של 5 עד 10 מ"מ בשנה לאורך [[גבול מתכנס]] {{אנ|Convergent boundary}}. הממשק של אזור הפחת נקרע מדי פעם ב[[רעידת אדמה מגה-דחף|רעידות אדמה גדולות מגה-דחף]] כמו אלו ב[[רעידת האדמה בכרתים (365 לספירה)|-365]] {{אנ|365 Crete earthquake}} ו-[[1303 רעידת אדמה בכרתים|-1303]] {{אנ|1303 Crete earthquake}}. [[צונאמי]] נוצר לאורך [[התעלה ההלנית]] {{אנ|Hellenic Trench}} כאשר צד אחד של השבר נדחף לפתע כלפי מעלה, כשהוא מעביר טריליוני ליטרים של [[מי ים]] במהלך רעידת אדמה מסיבית.

== רעידת האדמה ==
רעידת האדמה בכרתים ב-1856 הייתה [[רעידת אדמה תוך לוחית|רעידת אדמה בעומק בינוני]] בעומק של 60 עד 90 ק"מ, בתוך [[הלוח האפריקאי]]. ככל הנראה מוקד הרעידה היה מול החוף הצפוני של כרתים.

== השפעות ==
רעידת האדמה גרמה לנזק נרחב לא רק ביוון, אלא גם ב[[המזרח התיכון|מזרח התיכון]] וב[[צפון אפריקה]]. הזמן המדויק של הרעידה היה בין 02:38 ל-02:45 בבוקר.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Zohar, M.|date=2017|title=A newly discovered historical earthquake or merely a chronological mistake? Report of Mary Eliza Rogers from October 10, 1856|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10950-017-9686-9|journal=Journal of Seismology|volume=21|issue=5|pages=1285–1290|bibcode=2017JSeis..21.1285Z|doi=10.1007/s10950-017-9686-9}}</ref>

רעידת האדמה הגיעה ל-11 [[עוצמה סייסמית]] ב[[סולם מרקאלי]] בכרתים. העיר [[הרקליון]] כמעט נהרסה, כשרק בין 18 ל-40 מתוך 3,600 הבתים נותרו על תילם. גם ערי החוף [[סיציה]] {{אנ|Sitia}} ו[[חאניה]] נפגעו קשות. בסך הכל נהרגו 538 מתושבי כרתים ו-637 בני אדם נפצעו. באי [[רודוס]] נהרסו כמה כפרים ושישים בני אדם מתו. גם האי [[סנטוריני]] ניזוק. ב[[קאסוס]] {{אנ|Kasos}} וב[[קרפאתוס]] נהרסו לחלוטין 8,000 בתים, והיו בהם 20 הרוגים.

ביוון הורגשה רעידת האדמה בערים [[יואנינה]] ו[[קיפריסיה]] {{אנ|Kyparissia}}.

=== מלטה ===
[[קובץ:Ghajn_Hadid_Tower_closer_view.JPG|ממוזער|250x250 פיקסלים| הריסות [[מגדל ג'אגן חאדיד]] {{אנ|Għajn Ħadid Tower}} לאחר רעידת האדמה.]]
באיים [[מלטה|המלטזיים]], רעידת האדמה הורגשה בעוצמה. הרעידה נמשכה בין 22 ל-60 שניות. סדקים גדולים נפערו בבתים ב[[ולטה]] ואזור [[גוזו]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Grech|first=Herman|date=2009|title=We cannot be complacent about earthquakes - expert|work=Times of Malta|url=https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/we-cannot-be-complacent-about-earthquakes-expert.252515|access-date=6 January 2021}}</ref> כיפת [[קתדרלת פאולוס הקדוש (מדינה)]] קרסה מבפנים, מה שגרם לנזקים של כ-1,000 [[לירה שטרלינג|ליש"ט]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Galea|first=Pauline|date=2007|title=Seismic history of the Maltese islands and considerations on seismic risk|url=https://www.annalsofgeophysics.eu/index.php/annals/article/viewFile/3053/3096|journal=Annals of Geophysics|volume=50|issue=6}}</ref> כנסייה אחרת, [[המסדר הכרמליתי|הכנסייה הכרמלית]], נפגעה גם היא.

רעידת האדמה הקריסה את מגדל ג'אגן חאדיד.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Iannucci, R., Martino, S., Paciello, A.|date=2020|title=Investigation of cliff instability at Għajn Ħadid Tower (Selmun Promontory, Malta) by integrated passive seismic techniques|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10950-019-09898-z|journal=Journal of Seismology|volume=24|issue=4|pages=897–916|bibcode=2020JSeis..24..897I|doi=10.1007/s10950-019-09898-z|access-date=16 April 2021}}</ref>

=== מצרים ===
הרעידה גרמה לנזק ב[[קהיר]]. שלוש רעידות הורגשו בין דקה לשתיים. 20 בתים קרסו וכ־200 בני אדם נפגעו. לפחות עשרה בני אדם מתו בקהיר. בעקבות התוצאות, במשך מספר ימים ניצולים רבים ישנו מחוץ לבתיהם מחשש להתמוטטות במהלך הלילה.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Badawy, A., Korrat, I., El-Hadidy, M.|date=2017|title=Update earthquake risk assessment in Cairo, Egypt|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10950-016-9621-5|journal=J Seismol|volume=21|issue=4|pages=571–589|bibcode=2017JSeis..21..571B|doi=10.1007/s10950-016-9621-5}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=25 January 2013|title=Earthquakes in Malta|url=https://vassallohistory.wordpress.com/earthquakes-in-malta/|access-date=4 January 2021|website=Maltese History & Heritage}}</ref>

ב[[אלכסנדריה]], רק חלק מהבנייה הישנה נפלה, אך לא היו השלכות משמעותיות על העיר. שני בני אדם נהרגו וכמה נפצעו.

סביב [[הדלתא של הנילוס|דלתת הנילוס]], קריסות בתים [[מינרט|וצריחים]] הרגו מספר נשים בעיירות [[טנטא|טנטה]] ו[[דמנהור]].{{הערה|שם=:1}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Simon Jusseret and Manuel Sintubin|date=2013|title=The Origins of an Old Myth: Sir Arthur Evans, Claude Schaeffer and the Seismic Destruction of Late Bronze Age Eastern Mediterranean Civilizations|url=https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/ssa/srl/article-abstract/84/1/94/144109/The-Origins-of-an-Old-Myth-Sir-Arthur-Evans-Claude?redirectedFrom=fulltext|journal=Seismological Research Letters|volume=84|issue=1|pages=94–100|doi=10.1785/0220120098}}</ref> מלחים מול החופים דיווחו שחשו את רעידת האדמה החזקה.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fxnnk2inWT0C&q=The+Seismicity+of+Egypt,+Arabia+and+the+Red+Sea:+A+Historical+Review|title=The Seismicity of Egypt, Arabia and the Red Sea: A Historical Review|date=1994|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9780521020251}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=N. N. Ambraseys, C. P. Melville, R. D. Adams|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fxnnk2inWT0C&q=The+Seismicity+of+Egypt,+Arabia+and+the+Red+Sea:+A+Historical+Review|title=The Seismicity of Egypt, Arabia and the Red Sea: A Historical Review|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1994|isbn=9780511524912|location=London|pages=69–70|doi=10.1017/CBO9780511524912}}</ref>

=== מקומות נוספים ===
רעד הורגש גם [[סירקוזה|בסירקיוז]] וב[[פוזאלו]] {{אנ|Pozzallo}}, [[סיציליה]], [[איטליה]], שם נגרם נזק קל.{{הערה|שם=:0}} הזעזוע גרם גם לנזק גם למקומות כמו [[סוריה]] [[ארץ ישראל|וישראל]]. עדי ראייה לאורך חופי [[חיפה]] ו[[לבנון]] דיווחו על גל "[[צונאמי]]" קטן.{{הערה|שם=PAPADOPOULOS}} השפעות רעידת האדמה הורגשו בכל אזור [[הים האדריאטי]] ו[[קפריסין]].

== בתרבות ==
בספר "חיי יום-יום בארץ-ישראל" (Domestic Life in Palestine) תיארה הסופרת [[מרי אליזה רוג'רס]] את חוויותיה מרעידת האדמה שהורגשה ב[[חיפה]] ואת הנזקים שגרמה הרעידה ביישובים בחופי [[הגליל]] ו[[לבנון]].{{הערה|עדותה נדונה במחקרו של מוטי זוהר מ[[אוניברסיטת חיפה]], "[https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017JSeis..21.1285Z/abstract תגלית חדשה או טעות בתאריך? דו"ח של מרי אליזה רוג'רס מיום 10 באוקטובר 1856 על רעידת אדמה בחיפה]" ([[2017]]) {{אנגלית}}}} אבל היא תארכה את האירוע בצורה לא נכונה, ללילה שבין 10 ל-11 ב[[אוקטובר]].{{הערה|שם=:2}}

english.title: 1856 Heraklion earthquake
english.wikitext:
{{Short description|Earthquake affecting the Ottoman Empire (present-day Crete, Greece)}} {{Infobox earthquake | name = 1856 Heraklion earthquake | duration = 2 minutes | coordinates = {{coord|35.5|26.0|display=inline, title}} | pushpin_map = #Greece #Mediterranean | timestamp = 1856-10-12 00:45 | local_date = 11–12 October 1856 | local_time = 02:38 am or 02:45 am [[Eastern European Time|EET]] | depth = 61–100 km | magnitude = 7.7–8.3 {{M|w|link=yes}} | type = Intraplate | areas_affected = [[Mediterranean Sea]]
{{flatlist| * [[Greece]] * [[Malta]] * [[Sicily]] * [[Anatolia]] * [[Cyprus]] * [[Egypt]] * [[Palestine (region)|Palestine]] }} | max_intensity = {{MMI|11}}–{{MMI|XII}} | tsunami = Unlikely | aftershocks = Yes | casualties = 600+ dead
600+ injured | pre_1900 = yes }} The '''1856 Heraklion earthquake''', also known as the '''Crete earthquake''' or '''Rhodes earthquake''', occurred on the morning of October 12 at 02:45 am local time.{{Cite journal |author1=Y. Altinok |author2=B. Alpar |author3=N. Özer |author4=C. Gazioglu|date=2005|title=1881 and 1949 earthquakes at the Chios-Cesme Strait (Aegean Sea) and their relation to tsunamis|url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00299270/document|journal=Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences|publisher=Copernicus Publications s on behalf of the European Geosciences Union|volume=5|issue=5|pages=717–725|doi=10.5194/nhess-5-717-2005|bibcode=2005NHESS...5..717A|s2cid=14989944 |doi-access=free }} This extremely catastrophic [[earthquake]] had an estimated magnitude of 7.7 to 8.3 at a depth of approximately 61 to 100 km.{{Cite web|title=Seismicity Catalog (550 B.C. – 2010)|url=http://geophysics.geo.auth.gr/the_seisnet/WEBSITE_2005/station_index_en.html|access-date=4 January 2021|website=Seismological Station|location=Aristotle University of Thessaloniki|archive-date=21 March 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080321121735/http://geophysics.geo.auth.gr/the_seisnet/WEBSITE_2005/station_index_en.html|url-status=dead}} The earthquake was felt over a very wide area extending from [[Sicily]], [[Italy]] to the [[Levant]] and [[North Africa]].{{Cite book|author1=Papadopoulos, Gerassimos |author2=Vassilopoulos, A.|title=Tsunami Research at the End of a Critical Decade|publisher=Kluwer|year=2001|isbn=978-90-481-5909-3|pages=119–183|chapter=Historical and Archaeological Evidence of Earthquakes and Tsunamis Felt in the Kythira Strait, Greece.}} On the [[Greece|Greek]] island of [[Crete]], the effects of the earthquake were cataclysmic, over 500 bodies were recovered in the city of [[Heraklion]]. Shockwaves from the earthquake were felt intensely, covering all of the [[Ottoman Empire]]; present-day [[Turkey]], [[Cyprus]] and the [[Middle East]] where damage and human losses were reported. In [[Malta]], the [[Għajn Ħadid Tower]]—a coastal watchtower built around the year 1638—was severely damaged in the earthquake, when its upper floor collapsed. In [[Cairo]], Egypt, the earthquake destroyed buildings, created [[seiche]]s in canals, and killed several people. Off the Egyptian and [[Italy|Italian]] coasts, sailors reported feeling a [[seaquake]].{{Cite journal |author1=G. A. Papadopoulos |author2=E. Daskalaki |author3=A. Fokaefs |author4=N. Giraleas |title=Tsunami hazard in the eastern Mediterranean Sea: Strong earthquakes and tsunamis in the west Hellenic Arc and Trench system |url=http://www.seahellarc.gr/files/20091123154851Papadopoulos_et_al.JET.pdf|journal=Journal of Earthquake and Tsunami|access-date=2021-01-04|archive-date=2016-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304001548/http://www.seahellarc.gr/files/20091123154851Papadopoulos_et_al.JET.pdf|url-status=dead}} == Tectonic background == Along the southern coast of the [[Dodecanese|Dodecanese Islands]], [[Rhodes]], Crete and the [[Ionian Islands]], the [[African plate]] made of oceanic crust is [[Subduction|subducting]] beneath the [[Aegean Sea plate]] (part of the [[Eurasian plate]]) along a [[Convergent boundary|convergent plate boundary]] at a rate of 5 to 10 mm/yr. The interface of the subduction zone occasionally ruptures in large [[megathrust earthquake]]s such as those in [[365 Crete earthquake|365]] and [[1303 Crete earthquake|1303]]. Tsunamis are produced along the [[Hellenic Trench]] as one side of the fault is suddenly thrust upwards, displacing trillions of liters of seawater during a massive earthquake. == Earthquake == The Heraklion earthquake of 1856 was an [[intermediate-depth earthquake]] with a [[hypocenter]] [[Depth of focus (tectonics)|depth]] of 60 to 90 km, occurring on a fault within the subducting [[African plate]].{{Cite journal|last=Papazachos, B.|date=1996|title=Large seismic faults in the Hellenic arc|journal=Annals of Geophysics|volume=39|issue=5|doi=10.4401/ag-4023|doi-access=free}} The epicenter is most likely located off the northern coast of Crete, based on evaluating where the strongest isoseismic contours were. For a moment magnitude 7.7 ({{M|w}}) event, the estimated fault dimensions is 64 km × 64 km at a depth of 90 km beneath the [[Aegean Sea]] while an 8.1–8.3 {{M|w}}would involve a 120 km × 120 km fault rupture at a deeper depth of 130 km.{{Cite journal |author1=Kkallas, Charalampos |author2=C. Papazachos |author3=A. Skarlatoudis |author4=Chrysanthi, Ventouzi |author5=D. Boore |author6=B. Margaris.|date=2018|title=Explaining the large anomalous damage patterns of large (M7+) intermediate-depth earthquakes in the southern Aegean Sea|url=https://www.daveboore.com/pubs_online/16eceE_KKALLAS_final2.pdf|journal=16th European Conference on: Earthquake Engineering Thessaloniki}} == Effects == The earthquake caused widespread damage not just in Greece, but in the [[Middle East]] and [[North Africa]], where additional deaths and damage was reported. An exact time of occurrence is still debated between 02:38 am or 02:45 am.{{Cite journal|last=Zohar, M.|date=2017|title=A newly discovered historical earthquake or merely a chronological mistake? Report of Mary Eliza Rogers from October 10, 1856|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10950-017-9686-9|journal=Journal of Seismology|volume=21|issue=5|pages=1285–1290|doi=10.1007/s10950-017-9686-9|bibcode=2017JSeis..21.1285Z|s2cid=135012529|url-access=subscription}} === Greece === The earthquake reached [[Seismic intensity scales|XI (''Extreme'')]] on the [[Mercalli intensity scale]] in the central part of Crete. The city of [[Heraklion]] was almost destroyed, with only 18 or 40 of the 3,600 houses left standing. The seaside cities of [[Sitia]] and [[Chania]] were also severely damaged. A total of 538 inhabitants of Crete were killed while 637 persons were injured. On the island of [[Rhodes]], several villages were destroyed and the coast experienced uplift. Ground failures were widely observed amidst the destruction. Sixty people died on the island. The island of [[Santorini|Thera]] also reported some damage.{{citation|title=Significant Earthquake Database|url=https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/hazel/view/hazards/earthquake/event-more-info/2005|author=National Geophysical Data Center / World Data Service (NGDC/WDS)|publisher=[[National Geophysical Data Center]], [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration|NOAA]]|doi=10.7289/V5TD9V7K|year = 1972|type = Data Set}} In [[Kasos]] and [[Karpathos]], 8,000 homes were wiped-out, and there were 20 deaths.{{Cite book |author1=Simon Jusseret |author2=Manuel Sintubin|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_JInDwAAQBAJ&q=Cairo+earthquake+1856&pg=PA179|title=Earthquakes and Minoan Crete: breaking the myth through interdisciplinarity|date = 9 June 2017|publisher=Leuven University Press|location=Leuven|publication-place=Belgium|pages=178–180|isbn = 9789462701052}} On mainland Greece, the earthquake was felt in the cities of [[Ioannina]] and [[Kyparissia]]. === Malta === [[File:Ghajn_Hadid_Tower_closer_view.JPG|thumb|250x250px|Ruins of the [[Għajn Ħadid Tower]] after the earthquake.]] In the [[Maltese Islands]], the earthquake was felt much stronger than most earthquakes from Greece when felt on the islands, making this very unusual and of interest to many seismologists. The quake disrupted the night and woke everyone on the island. The shaking lasted between 22 and 60 seconds, causing many residents to lose their balance and threw down many items in houses. Large cracks developed in the homes of some places such as [[Valletta]] and [[Gozo Region]].{{Cite news|last=Grech|first=Herman|date=2009|title=We cannot be complacent about earthquakes – expert|work=Times of Malta|url=https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/we-cannot-be-complacent-about-earthquakes-expert.252515|access-date=6 January 2021}} Many churches had cracks in the walls and domes and had hanging crucifixes falling off. In some cases, the damage was more serious, some churches experiencing a total collapse. The dome of [[St Paul's Cathedral, Mdina|Saint Paul's Cathedral in Mdina]] collapsed from the inside, which caused some [[British pound|£]]1,000 in damage.{{Cite journal|last=Galea|first=Pauline|date=2007|title=Seismic history of the Maltese islands and considerations on seismic risk|url=https://www.annalsofgeophysics.eu/index.php/annals/article/viewFile/3053/3096|journal=Annals of Geophysics|volume=50|issue=6}} Another church, the [[Carmelite Church]], had its [[steeple]] rebuilt because the earthquake had damaged it so severely. Damage to structures corresponded to intensity VII, higher than expected for the 1,000 km distance from the earthquake in Greece. A typical earthquake should only be felt with intensities IV–V. The occurrence of very strong shaking is likely attributed to [[long period ground motion]].{{cite journal |author1=Pauline Galea |title=Seismic history of the Maltese islands and considerations on seismic risk |journal=Annals of Geophysics |date=December 2007 |volume=50 |issue=6 |location=University of Malta}} It was this earthquake that collapsed the [[Għajn Ħadid Tower]].{{cite journal |author1=Iannucci, R. |author2=Martino, S. |author3=Paciello, A. |title=Investigation of cliff instability at Għajn Ħadid Tower (Selmun Promontory, Malta) by integrated passive seismic techniques |journal=Journal of Seismology |date=2020 |volume=24 |issue=4 |pages=897–916 |doi=10.1007/s10950-019-09898-z |bibcode=2020JSeis..24..897I |s2cid=209672820 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10950-019-09898-z |access-date=16 April 2021|url-access=subscription }} An eyewitness present at the tower one month before the earthquake said large cracks opened in the ground around the tower.{{cite web |author1=Simon Mifsud |title=Għajn Ħadid Tower and Aħrax Tower |url=http://www.militaryarchitecture.com:80/index.php/Fortifications/ghajn-hadid-tower-and-ahrax-tower.html |website=MilitaryArchitecture.com |access-date=16 April 2021}} === Egypt === In [[Cairo]], the shaking was still perceivable and strong enough to cause damage. Shaking intensity in the [[Egypt]]ian capital reached VII–VIII. Three distinct shocks were felt with durations between one and two minutes. Twenty homes collapsed and another 200 were affected, while some 20 mosques were also crippled. [[Seiches]] in canals caused water to splash all over while clocks stopped working as a result of the ground motions. At least ten people died in the city. Following the aftermath, many survivors slept outside their homes for fear of a collapse during the night for several days.{{Cite journal |author1=Badawy, A. |author2=Korrat, I. |author3=El-Hadidy, M.|date=2017|title=Update earthquake risk assessment in Cairo, Egypt|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10950-016-9621-5|journal=J Seismol|volume=21|issue=4|pages=571–589|doi=10.1007/s10950-016-9621-5|bibcode=2017JSeis..21..571B|s2cid=133402193|url-access=subscription}}{{Cite web|title=Earthquakes in Malta|url=https://vassallohistory.wordpress.com/earthquakes-in-malta/|access-date=4 January 2021|website=Maltese History & Heritage|date=25 January 2013 }} In [[Alexandria]], only some old construction fell but there were no major implications to the city. Two people were killed and some injuries were sustained to people. Around the [[Nile Delta]], collapses of homes and falling [[minaret]]s killed an additional number of people in the towns of [[Tanta]] and [[Damanhur]].{{Cite journal|last=Simon Jusseret and Manuel Sintubin|date=2013|title=The Origins of an Old Myth: Sir Arthur Evans, Claude Schaeffer and the Seismic Destruction of Late Bronze Age Eastern Mediterranean Civilizations|url=https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/ssa/srl/article-abstract/84/1/94/144109/The-Origins-of-an-Old-Myth-Sir-Arthur-Evans-Claude?redirectedFrom=fulltext|journal=Seismological Research Letters|volume=84|issue=1|pages=94–100|doi=10.1785/0220120098|bibcode=2013SeiRL..84...94J |s2cid=110029713 |url-access=subscription}} In other parts of the delta, many residents found it difficult to stand, which terrified many. Ground motions were strong enough to shift furniture and cause water in tanks to slosh around. Sailors off the coasts reported feeling the strong earthquake as well.{{Cite book|date=1994|title=The Seismicity of Egypt, Arabia and the Red Sea: A Historical Review|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fxnnk2inWT0C&q=The+Seismicity+of+Egypt,+Arabia+and+the+Red+Sea:+A+Historical+Review|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9780521020251}}{{Cite book |author1=N. N. Ambraseys |author2=C. P. Melville |author3=R. D. Adams|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fxnnk2inWT0C&q=The+Seismicity+of+Egypt,+Arabia+and+the+Red+Sea:+A+Historical+Review|title=The Seismicity of Egypt, Arabia and the Red Sea: A Historical Review|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1994|isbn=9780511524912|location=London|pages=69–70|doi=10.1017/CBO9780511524912}} === Elsewhere === Shaking was also felt in [[Syracuse, Sicily|Syracuse]] and [[Pozzallo]], [[Sicily]], Italy where some minor damage occurred. The shock also caused damage to places like [[Syria]] and [[Palestine (region)|Palestine]]. Eyewitnesses along the coasts of [[Haifa]] and [[Lebanon]] reported a small "tsunami" wave. Effects from the earthquake was felt in the entire [[Adriatic Sea]] region and Cyprus. == Legacy == In the book ''Domestic Life in Palestine'', author [[Mary Eliza Rogers]] described her experience of the strong tremors in [[Haifa]], Israel but she dated the event incorrectly between the night of 10 and 11 October. == See also == * [[List of earthquakes in Greece]] * [[List of earthquakes in Turkey]] * [[List of earthquakes in Egypt]] * [[Seismic risk in Malta]] == References == {{Reflist}} {{Earthquakes in Greece}} {{Earthquakes in Turkey}} {{Earthquakes in the Levant}} [[Category:1856 earthquakes]] [[Category:1850s disasters in Europe]] [[Category:1856 in Greece]] [[Category:1856 in the Ottoman Empire]] [[Category:1850s disasters in Asia]] [[Category:1856 disasters in Africa]] [[Category:19th-century disasters in the Ottoman Empire]] [[Category:October 1856]] [[Category:Earthquakes in Greece]] [[Category:Earthquakes in Europe]] [[Category:Natural disasters in Malta]] [[Category:Earthquakes in Turkey]] [[Category:Earthquakes in the Middle East]] [[Category:Earthquakes in Egypt]] [[Category:Earthquakes in Israel]] [[Category:Earthquakes in Palestine]] [[Category:Earthquakes in Syria]] [[Category:Earthquakes in the Levant]] [[Category:Earthquakes in Crete]] [[Category:Heraklion]]
